stories.headline: Fair Moderation, Equitable Access, and AI: arXiv’s Updated Rate Limit Policy
stories.dek: The preprint repository has capped author submissions at two per calendar month across categories, citing moderation pressure and the rapid rise in submissions.
tldr: arXiv's updated policy permits each author up to two submissions per calendar month across all categories.
The repository says submissions reached 40,363 in September 2026, compared with 20,569 in September 2024.
The cap took effect on October 1 as a stopgap while arXiv reviews moderation tools and submission practices.

body.text: arXiv's October 1 policy sets a limit of two submissions per author per calendar month across categories and retains a separate limit of three active submissions. The organization describes the change as a temporary measure while it considers longer-term submission practices and moderation capacity.

arXiv reported 40,363 submissions in September 2026, roughly double its September 2024 total of 20,569, and said the month generated almost 9,000 support tickets. The figures are the repository's own account of the workload behind the policy change.

stories.whyItMatters: The rule turns moderation capacity into a direct constraint on researchers' distribution schedules across every subject area hosted by arXiv. Because the repository calls the cap a stopgap, its effects and any later replacement will matter to labs and conference workflows, but the announcement does not yet establish how moderation outcomes will change.
stories.editorNote: The policy and workload figures are attributed to arXiv; The Register independently reports the change. The edition is intentionally narrow because the remaining collected items lacked comparable primary-source support.

stories.headline: AI giants 'not being nearly careful enough,' warns outgoing OpenAI safety engineer
stories.dek: An outgoing OpenAI safety engineer’s warning about company safety practices was reported by Deutsche Welle and Investing.com.
tldr: An outgoing OpenAI safety engineer warned that AI companies were not being sufficiently careful, according to Deutsche Welle.
Investing.com separately reported the employee’s departure and a call to end a trial-and-error approach.
The two reports frame the departure as a safety-governance signal, while neither headline establishes a company-wide policy change.

body.text: Deutsche Welle reported the engineer’s warning that AI companies were “not being nearly careful enough.”

Investing.com also reported the OpenAI safety employee’s departure and described the message as a call to move beyond trial and error. The available headlines do not establish a resulting change in OpenAI policy.

stories.whyItMatters: The reports put internal safety governance back in focus as frontier AI companies scale deployment. The coverage documents an employee’s criticism; it does not by itself show that OpenAI changed its practices.
stories.editorNote: Added from two independently hosted reports. Claims are limited to what their headlines establish.
